claim: The 'Au fil de l'Our' loop starts at Our church (Paliseul), is 11.5 km with 222 m ascent (max 347 m, min 259 m), classified easy, ~3 h 9 min — the signed loop closest to the village.
quote: Distance: 11.5 km ... Maximum altitude of 347 m, minimum of 259 m, with 222 m uphill and 219 m downhill gain ... Starting Point: Church of Our (Paliseul) ... approximately 3 hours and 9 minutes

claim: Paliseul commune has 32 marked walking circuits plus 9 mountain-bike circuits on its 2021 map, sold for €7.50 at the Syndicat d'Initiatives (Grand Place 7).
quote: La nouvelle carte des promenades de Paliseul, édition 2021, contient 32 circuits pédestres balisés et 9 circuits VTT balisés

claim: The classic Tombeau du Géant family loop from Botassart is 6.5 km, easy, with free parking at the viewpoint and a small bar on-site, taking in the Lyru viewpoint and Rocher des Gattes.
quote: 6,5 km ... facile ... Un parking gratuit est disponible au point de vue du tombeau du géant ... Un petit bar au point de vue est disponible ... le point de vue de Lyru ... le rocher des Gattes

claim: An even shorter Tombeau du Géant variant via Moulin du Rivage is 4.81 km, 130 m gain, ~1 h 24, rated easy, but can be slippery after rain.
quote: Distance: 4.81 km ... Elevation Gain: 130 m ... Duration: 1 hour 24 minutes ... Easy ... requiring sturdy hiking boots as sections can be slippery, especially after rain

claim: The big 17.5 km Tombeau du Géant adventure loop has ~700 m elevation, two Semois river crossings, is hard, only feasible May–Oct in low water, parking at Moulin du Rivage.
quote: 17.5 km as a loop with approximately 700 m of elevation gain ... Two Semois river crossings ... May–Oct when water levels remain manageable ... do not underestimate how hard this hike is

claim: The Échelles de Rochehaut loop is 4.7 km, ~1 h 30, rated difficult, with metal ladders up steep cliffs; sturdy shoes required and not advised after heavy rain.
quote: Distance: 4.7 km ... 1 hour 30 minutes ... Difficile ... appropriate hiking shoes, as certain passages can be slippery ... climbing metal ladders on steep rocky cliffs

claim: The combined Échelles + Crêtes de Frahan circuit from Rochehaut is the regional benchmark hike, with hundreds of AllTrails reviews highlighting its scrambles and Frahan ridge panoramas.
quote: Rochehaut - Les Échelles - Crêtes de Frahan, Luxembourg, Belgium - 578 Reviews

claim: The Bouillon '12 viewpoints' circuit is 14.62 km with +665 m, medium difficulty, ~6 h, and chains Belvédère de Bouillon, Pic du Diable, Tombeau du Géant, Rocher du Pendu and Ramonette.
quote: Distance: 14.62 km ... Elevation Gain: +665 m ... Difficulty: Medium ... Pic du Diable (km 4.08) ... Augustins/Tombeau du Géant (km 6.54) ... Rocher du Pendu (km 8.93)

claim: Pic du Diable, a rocky belvedere over the Semois plain west of Bouillon, is a stand-alone POI reachable by several waymarked routes including an 18.7 km Belvédère d'Auclin – Pic du Diable loop (~5 h 23).
quote: From the viewpoint 'Pic du Diable' you can enjoy a sweeping view over the Semois river plains ... a difficult circuit from Bouillon called 'Belvédère d'Auclin – Le Pic du Diable' covers 18.7 km and takes about 5 hours and 23 minutes

claim: The Maison du Tourisme de Bouillon lists the canonical local viewpoints — Chaire à Prêcher (Corbion), Tombeau du Géant (Botassart), Belvédère Panorama, Rocher de Baimont/Ramonette, Frahan loop, Jambon de la Semois (Membre) and Roche à Saloru — but does not list a 'Roche à 7 heures' in Bouillon.
quote: Chaire à Prêcher - Corbion ... Tombeau du Géant - Botassart ... Belvédère Panorama - Bouillon ... Frahan & Semois Loop - Rochehaut ... Jambon de la Semois - Membre ... Roche à Saloru - Membre

claim: The famous 'Roche à Sept Heures' is in Monthermé, French Ardennes — a Meuse-valley belvedere named for the 7 o'clock sun-flash on the cliff, not a Bouillon-area site.
quote: The name Roche à Sept Heures comes from the fact that at seven o'clock, the sun illuminating this rocky spur gives it a very visible shine ... overlooks the town of Monthermé and opens a beautiful window onto the bends of the Meuse

claim: Roche aux Éperviers at Bouillon is a fitted belvedere with stairs and a safety rail above the 'longest meander created by the Semois', overlooking Botassart and Poupehan woods.
quote: improved access pathway with stairs and safety railings ... Botassart and Poupehan woodlands ... la plus longue boucle créée par la Semois

claim: GR 16 'Sentier de la Semois' is 209 km from Arlon to Monthermé, marked with the standard white-red blazes, with a 7th-edition topo-guide at €23.
quote: Total Length: 209 kilometers ... Endpoints: Arlon to Monthermé ... Seventh edition ... Price: €23.00

claim: The Trans-Semoisienne is a 184 km source-to-mouth multi-use route co-signed with GR16 white-red blazes in Belgium; its own yellow-triangle marking is for horses and MTB, and between Auby-sur-Semois and Bouillon it shortcuts the meanders via tarmac while GR16 hugs the river.
quote: 184 km total ... Volunteers maintain white-and-red blazes (GR 16 standard markings) ... a yellow horizontal triangle with the Contrat de rivière Semois/Semoy logo ... intended for equestrians and mountain bikers ... Trans-Semoisienne cuts across several Semois meanders via asphalt roads between Auby-sur-Semois and Bouillon

claim: 'Au gré de la Semois' is an easy 8.3 km riverside walk from Porte de France in Bouillon, marked red rectangle (BN #41), passing the Épine suspended footbridge to Cordemois Abbey — a strong family option.
quote: Distance: 8.3 km ... Difficulty: Easy ... Porte de France 1 à 6830 Bouillon ... longe la Semois via un magnifique sentier ... red rectangles (trail BN #41)

claim: The Parc national Vallée de la Semois runs a 2026 calendar of around sixty guided walks between April and October, useful for late-May visitors looking for ranger-led options.
quote: Un calendrier de balades guidées 2026 ... une soixantaine de sorties prévues ... entre les mois d'avril et d'octobre
